description.short_caption: Clinical photograph of a swollen, discolored lower leg with skin changes.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a lower leg with significant swelling, erythema, and areas of dark discoloration. The skin appears tense and shiny, with some areas of bruising or necrosis. There are faint markings on the skin, possibly for tracking the progression of swelling or discoloration. The findings suggest a severe soft tissue infection or vascular compromise.

Case_02048/figure3.jpg.source_caption: Gram stain of blood culture. (Photo by Lynn Bry, M.D.)

description.short_caption: Gram stain of blood culture showing gram-negative bacilli.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a Gram stain of a blood culture specimen. Numerous pink-staining, rod-shaped bacteria (gram-negative bacilli) are visible, indicating a gram-negative bacterial infection. The background is relatively clear, suggesting a high concentration of bacteria in the sample. The staining technique highlights the characteristic morphology and gram-negative cell wall properties of the organisms.
visible_findings: pink-staining rods consistent with gram-negative bacilli
clear background with no visible host cells

description.short_caption: Bilateral lower leg discoloration with erythema, swelling, and necrotic changes.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph shows both lower legs of a patient. The left leg exhibits extensive erythema, swelling, and dark discoloration suggestive of necrosis, with a clear demarcation line. The right leg shows milder erythema and discoloration. The findings are consistent with a severe soft tissue infection, possibly necrotizing fasciitis or cellulitis with ischemic changes. The patient is positioned supine, and the legs are exposed for examination.
visible_findings: erythema and swelling of the left leg
dark discoloration and necrotic changes on the left leg
milder erythema and discoloration on the right leg
clear demarcation line on the left leg
